newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Victoria to sell 6 gas companies in 98.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Victoria to sell 6 gas companies in 98.

text.p: The state government of Victoria said on Wednesday it would sell its six newly-created gas companies sequentially between April and August 1998.
The companies would each be sold in pairs of one distributor and one retailer, Victorian Treasury official Peter Troughton said.
"The sale of the three stapled retail and distribution gas businesses is scheduled for between April and August next year," Troughton said.
Troughton said a roadshow for the sales would be launched in February.
The sales would be conducted along the same lines as the state's recent sell-off of its electricity industry, he said
Funds from the sales would be used to pay off state debt and achieve a AAA credit rating, he said.
The three new gas distribution companies, Stratus Networks, Westar and Multinet are responsible for delivering gas to consumers and connecting new customers to the gas pipeline.
The three retailers, Kinetic Energy, Energy 21 and Ikon Energy have been allocated customers in seperate geographical areas of the state in the lead up to privatisation.
